account:
It is ten o'clock on day 0, and I have reached the plaza for my scheduled market walk. The clearest unusual report is that the builder shouted near the inn, asking the innkeeper where they were and whether they could meet privately. I heard an indistinct distant shout earlier; Townsfolk 30 supplied the words. I do not yet know whether they actually met or what they want to discuss. A private meeting could be ordinary business, so this is a lead, not evidence of wrongdoing or a scheme excluding me.

Townsfolk 10 and 30 also reported that the baker carried a sack of wheat at the bakery. That sounds consistent with ordinary baking, and I have no evidence connecting it to the builder's request.

The secretary says no correspondence or reports of unusual business have arrived. My appointment book schedules tea at fifteen hundred with an unnamed neighbour in an unspecified east-bank dockside cottage. The secretary has agreed to verify the host and location. That vagueness needs resolving, but I cannot yet connect the appointment to anything suspicious. The secretary initially asked me for engagements despite the existing book, then put the book back after we clarified the schedule; I have no basis to treat that as deliberate concealment.

For now, I want to learn discreetly what the builder and innkeeper are discussing while keeping my appointments. There is not yet enough information to say what, if anything, unusual is being organized.
